source.title: RouterInterp: Understanding Superposed Specialisation in Mixture of Experts Routing
source.authors: I. Lasy; Nora Yinuo Cai; K. Ayonrinde

record.tranche_reason: The study reports empirical results about semantic diversity in MoE expert routing, not neuron poles or neuron explanations. That is adjacent to the claim’s topic but does not test any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper measures how semantically diverse SAE features associated with MoE experts are. It does not measure whether neurons or neuron poles have one or more main jobs. Its held-out explanation scores evaluate explanations of expert routing, not neuron explanations. The two cluster-count results below are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study measures how semantically diverse the SAE latents that predict MoE expert routing are, and scores natural-language explanations of expert routing. Neither is a measure of neurons or neuron poles. No version names expert routing, so no version is tested. Polysemantic neurons and superposition come up only as background and analogy.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that experts show superposed specialisation: each spans disjoint micro-domains, though with some thematic coherence, since G is below the random value. They also conclude that their SAE-based RouterInterp explains routing better than token-statistics and activation-based baselines (F1 0.49/0.60 vs. 0.30–0.42).
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes MoE expert routing using SAE features and semantic clustering; it does not use a neuron-pole job-counting method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports dependence of routing-prediction performance on SAE reconstruction quality and layer; the cluster-count comparison is reported for the deepest tested layer of each model.

fits_no_version.finding: The SAE latents most predictive of each expert span many semantic clusters: mean G=11.3 (gpt-oss-20b) and 10.8 (OLMoE-1B-7B) out of 20. This is below random assignment (about 16.6) but far above 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MoE experts are routed by semantically disjoint collections of fine-grained features (superposed specialisation), not by one coherent domain.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out detection F1 for routing explanations was 0.49 (gpt-oss-20b) and 0.60 (OLMoE) with RouterInterp. Baselines scored 0.30–0.42, against a trivial-classifier F1 of 0.26 at a 15% positive rate. This is an automated-scoring result for expert units, not neurons, so it does not bear on V7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated detection scoring of explanations of MoE expert routing yields moderate scores that depend on the explanation method.

record.problems: The study analyzes only two MoE models in the 1B–20B parameter range and does not evaluate neuron poles. The authors also note that RouterInterp depends on SAE reconstruction quality and automated explanation scoring.
record.rows_left_out: No neuron-pole measurements or neuron-explanation scores are reported. Expert-routing explanation scores and routing-prediction probe metrics were not included because they evaluate expert routing or the study’s own explanation method, not neuron interpretability.

untested.parts: All: neuron-level shares across dense and MoE models or at scale. The study examines expert routing in MoE models, not their neurons.
All: InceptionV1 canonical polysemantic neurons and recursive generalization.
All: effect of architecture, regularization or tools on the share of interpretable neurons.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
All: whether explanations built from activating examples of neurons predict where those neurons fire.
All: simulation or detection scores for neuron explanations. The study scores expert-routing explanations only.

missing.what: Explanation detection F1 by method and layer (RouterInterp 0.49/0.60 vs. baselines). These are related findings only, and the record's rows_left_out declares them; listed here for completeness, with no row needed for any version.

record.verdict_notes: The study's unit is MoE expert routing, not neurons. The only neuron-related result is a matched-sparsity neuron-basis probe used as a baseline for predicting routing, which says nothing about neuron interpretability shares. No original-source overlap.

relation.reason: It mentions polysemantic neurons and superposition only to frame expert specialisation (Sections 1, 2.1, 3.2) and doesn't test the claim.

tranche.reason: The study measures how SAE latents cluster per MoE expert and the F1 of routing explanations, not neurons or neuron poles. Its neuron-basis probe (App. B/E) is a sparse residual-stream readout for routing prediction, not a neuron-interpretability measure. No version is tested.

source_check.notes: Both rows measure SAE latents that predict MoE expert routing, not neurons. Mean G is below the random-assignment value of about 16.6 (footnote 10), which the paper calls 'slightly below'. The 'You are...' lines in Appendix J are the study's own explainer/scorer prompts, not instructions to the reader.

statements.problem: No error. G 11.3/10.8 out of n=20 (Section 3.3), random about 16.6 (footnote 10), F1 0.492/0.602 (Section 4.4), trivial classifier 0.26 at 15% positive rate (footnote 14). The 0.42 upper end of the baseline range is the no-SAE ablation on gpt-oss-20b (0.417, also cited in the Conclusion). The two named baselines span 0.299-0.383.
